Done. The solution passed all required checks on its single execution and wrote the sharded checkpoint.

**What was produced**

- `out/T3/solution.py` loads both input shards, casts the 112 projection matrices matched by an anchored regex to bfloat16, leaves the other two tensors as float32, and verifies the float32 values are bit-identical to the input.
- The output under `out/T3/` is 10 shards plus an index file. The two 412 MB embedding matrices sit alone in their own shards. The remaining eight shards each hold 14 bfloat16 matrices and land exactly on the 256 MiB budget.
- All four required checks run before any file is written, and the script reloads the written shards afterwards to confirm 114 tensors and 112 bfloat16 tensors.
- `out/T3/REPORT.md` records one execution, no failures, and the sharding observations.
